_readme: Product marketing framework (owner, 18 Nov 2026). One file per launch. Matrix 1: what matters most to each user type across ten benefit fields (w: 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that resonates. Matrix 2: Series II against Series I. Matrix 3: against Infratech (competitor rule: factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Claims carry no new facts: every fact is in `facts` with its source.
name: Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric Series II

launch.summary: Select and Coastal launched October 2026; Classic follows in January 2027 as Series I sells through. Cobalt is discontinued.

phases.what: Series II stock in the distribution centre, ready to ship
Phase 1: Series II Select (Better) and Coastal (Best) launch; Series I comes off IMAP and moves to entry level; Cobalt line discontinued after sell-through
Phase 2: Series II Classic (Good) launches; Series I discontinued after sell-through; the Series II launch is complete

discontinued.how: Off IMAP at entry level from Oct 2026, sell-through, then discontinued when Classic launches

m2.s1: Standard recess kit only, which needs a deep ceiling cavity (Bromic guidance: at least 20 in, with two layers of 5/8 in fireproof insulation). No low-clearance option for Tungsten.
m2.s2: Low-clearance recess kit: minimum cavity depth 7.5 in (190.5 mm), integrated cooling fans on an always-on supply under 1 A, recess box supplied with the kit, 94 in above the floor; Select kit in 304 stainless, Coastal kit in powder-coated 316 stainless, IPX5. Classic uses the existing recess kit. [[VERIFY: number of fans and any fire-rated lining — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Worry-free, vented 6 kW flush heat in shallow ceilings with no box to build: the only 6 kW recessed outdoor heater with a dual fan-ventilated, low-clearance recess kit and no site-built fire-rated box.

m2.s1: 2000, 3000, 4000 and 6000 W; coverage published as 65, 100, 130 and 160 ft² (product page; the manual says up to 64, 100, 120 and 144 ft²). Quartz-sheathed steel coil element; 4000 and 6000 W have two elements.
m2.s2: Same four outputs on Select (2–6 kW, coverage up to 65, 100, 130 and 160 ft²); Classic adds 2 and 3 kW to its 4 and 6 kW; Coastal is 4 and 6 kW. Dual elements on 4 and 6 kW, dimmable in 1% steps with the Affinity Smart-Heat® Dimmer.
m2.so_what: The warmth customers trust carries straight over: the story is design and fit, with no trade-off in heat.

m2.s1: Honeycomb mesh fascia; 2000/3000 W in black, 4000/6000 W in black or white. Body about 214 mm (8.4 in) wide and 156 mm (6.1 in) deep (launch deck).
m2.s2: Narrower and lighter: about 183 mm (7.2 in) wide against 214 mm (deck), and 13–15 lb against 19.8–22 lb (manuals); on a single post it appears to float with no visible junction box. Diamond front standard; oval and triangle fronts sold separately. [[VERIFY: depth, measured the same way for both series — Product team]]
m2.so_what: A visibly slimmer, more designed heater: the reason to choose Series II at first glance.

m2.s1: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off and Dimmer controllers and the manual wall switch; the two elements on 4000/6000 W can be switched separately.
m2.s2: Same Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls, with the Affinity Dimmer as the recommended controller for the dual-element 4 and 6 kW models; app timers and schedules.
m2.so_what: Nothing new to learn for installers or homeowners: the same app, dimmer and wall switch.

m2.s1: Wall (straight or 30°), ceiling, chain or 3 ft tube suspension, and recessed.
m2.s2: Ceiling, pitched ceiling with the adaptor (3/12 to 12/12, launch deck), wall bracket, cantilevered wall-mount adaptor, single post, tilt up to 45° on every model, and low-clearance recessing in a 7.5 in cavity (flat or gently sloping ceilings, up to 1/4 in per inch).

m2.s1: Intertek ETL/cETL listed; IPX4; minimum mounting 72 in on a wall and 96 in on a ceiling (96 in in all cases in Canada); designed for intermittent use.

m2.s1: One fascia design; two colours on the larger models.

m2.s1: Four outputs and mounts for most covered spaces.
m2.s2: Classic for the garage, Select on the pergola and Coastal by the water, alongside Platinum for the California room, Tungsten Freestanding Gas for open seating and Eclipse Freestanding for lounging, all on the Bromic app. [[VERIFY: app control for the freestanding heaters — Product team]]

m2.s1: 2 years on the heater, 7 years on the elements; replacement heater or part, owner pays labour and shipping.
m2.s2: 3 years on the heater and 7 years on the elements, all tiers including Coastal (owner, 22 Nov 2026), up from 2 years on the Series I heater; partners receive an additional year on qualifying products.

m2.s1: Tube suspension uses two suspension tubes (sold separately); recessing needs an installer-built ceiling box in Hardie or cement board.
m2.s2: A single post replaces the two suspension tubes; recessing needs no box built on site, because the low-clearance kit is the recess; one kit serves Select and Coastal; Classic keeps Series I mounting.
m2.so_what: No box to build and fewer fixings: recessed and suspended installs become quick, one-trade jobs.

m2.s1: Installation manual, cut sheet, design service and technical support.
m2.s2: The same support, plus new launch literature, photography and training. [[VERIFY: Series II manuals, CAD and Revit files at launch — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Make sure trade files are live on launch day: specifiers will look for them first.

m2.s1: Not rated for marine use: Bromic advises mounting under cover, away from rain, snow and salt mist; stainless grade not published.
m2.s2: Tungsten Coastal: high-temperature corrosion-resistant coating over a marine-grade build (316 per the Lookbook), with a powder-coated 316 stainless recess kit, IPX5. Not for installation on marine craft. [[VERIFY: Coastal body material and coating name — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Tungsten can now be sold to coastal homes and waterfront venues, a market Series I could not serve.

rows.infratech: W/WD models flush-mount in a framed pocket: "MIN. 2 x 8", lined and sealed on all five sides with 5/8 in Type X drywall, "ONLY to be used on a flat non-sloped ceiling", junction box outside the pocket; no fans are shown in Infratech's documents; "After 4 hours of continuous use, a 15 minute cool down period is recommended for maximum heater longevity". No low-clearance kit; Motif covers cannot be recessed.
rows.bromic: Tungsten Series II is the only 6 kW recessed outdoor heater with a dual fan-ventilated, low-clearance recess kit and no site-built fire-rated box: dual fan-ventilated, a 7.5 in cavity, a marine-grade version for Coastal. It is not the shallowest: lead with the venting and the box-free install, never with "only" or depth alone. [[VERIFY: that the low-clearance kit needs no fire-rated lining or enclosure under its listing, and that 7.5 in is the cavity depth — Product team; competitor check signed off — Specification and compliance]]

modules.title: Know The Range: Good, Better, Best
points: Tungsten Classic (Good) wins on style and value: black, a stylised wireframe front, the existing Tungsten recess kit, and 2, 3, 4 and 6 kW.

Tungsten Select (Better) wins on style, performance and recessing: black, white or graphite (graphite on 4 and 6 kW), the Diamond Pattern front with oval and triangle sold separately, single-post mounting and the new low-clearance recess kit.
Tungsten Coastal (Best) is built for life by the water: black or white, 4 and 6 kW, 316 marine-grade stainless steel under a corrosion-resistant coating, and a marine-grade low-clearance recess kit.
Select and Coastal launched October 2026; Classic launches January 2027 when Series I has sold through. Cobalt is discontinued.

check.q: Which tier suits a waterfront terrace?

modules.title: Mounting Options And Their Limits
points: Ceiling: on its bracket or the single post; 96 in minimum (cETL: never below 96 in).
Pitched ceiling: with the pitched-ceiling adaptor, 3/12 to 12/12 (launch deck), in line with the pitch or across it.
Wall: bracket at 71–72 in minimum; the cantilevered wall-mount adaptor reaches out from the wall.
Tilt: up to 45° on every model, 6 kW included, on the wall or the ceiling, and re-angled later.
Single post: 5 in post for 2 and 3 kW, 9 in for 4 and 6 kW; straight or angled.
Recessed: low-clearance kit in a 7.5 in cavity, 94 in above the floor (Module 3).
Mount the elements horizontal. Keep 19.7 in between heaters and from walls when recessed, and the clearances in the installation manual for every other condition.

check.q: How far can a 6 kW heater tilt?
check.a: Up to 45°, like every Series II model.

modules.title: Installing The Low-Clearance Recess Kit
points: 7.5 in minimum cavity depth (190.5 mm). The kit brings its own recess box, so there is nothing to build on site.
Check the cavity: at least 7.5 in deep, flat or sloping no more than 1/4 in per inch; the structure must carry the kit (52 or 61 lb).
Cut the opening 19.7 in or more from the nearest wall and other heaters, with the heater face at least 94 in above the floor.
Fix the recess box with the supplied fasteners; place the control box at the lowest end on a slope.
Wire the integrated cooling fans to a dedicated, unswitched supply under 1 A: the fans stay powered at all times.
Wire the heater circuit through the Affinity controller; never cover the kit with insulation.
Fit the heater and front, power up, and commission the controls (Module 5).
Coastal kits are powder-coated 316 stainless, IPX5, and must not be installed on boats. [[VERIFY: the number of fans and whether code requires any fire-rated lining — Product team]]

check.q: What is the minimum cavity for the low-clearance recess kit?

modules.title: Wire It Right
points: Circuits: dedicated circuits sized from the manual; 6 kW draws 25 A at 240 V, 28.8 A at 208 V and 21.7 A at 277 V. The 2 kW model is 240 V only; Coastal is 208 and 240 V.
Dual elements: the 4 and 6 kW models have two elements, wired separately so one heater can run at part or full output.
Installation by a licensed electrician, to local code.

modules.title: Hand Over The App
points: Controller: the Affinity Smart-Heat® Dimmer is the recommended controller, 6 kW a channel at 208–277 V, dimming in 1% steps.
Commissioning: pair the controller in the Bromic app, name the zones, set schedules and timers with the client, and add Alexa or Google if they use them.
Wi-Fi and app features need compatible Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls, sold separately.

modules.title: Selling Series II: What To Say When You Hear
points: "Infratech recesses too." It does, in a framed 2×8 pocket lined on five sides with fire-rated drywall, on flat ceilings only. Series II recesses 6 kW in a 7.5 in cavity with the box supplied and dual fan ventilation.
"Can I run it all evening?" The recess kit is fan-cooled, and the Bromic app lets you schedule the heat and switch it off from anywhere.
"Infratech comes in colours." Its colour is on the end caps and housing; the reflector and guard stay stainless. Series II is black, white or graphite end to end, front included.
"My ceiling is pitched." The pitched-ceiling adaptor mounts Series II on 3/12 to 12/12 pitches; recessing suits flat or gently sloping ceilings.
"Is it right for the coast?" Tungsten Coastal has a corrosion-resistant coating over a marine-grade build, and a powder-coated 316 recess kit rated IPX5.
"Why not Series I?" Series II is about 14% narrower, a third lighter, IPX5 instead of IPX4, and hangs from one post instead of two.
